items.title: Karnataka High Court directs courts to accept digital copies of HC orders without insisting on physical certification
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has directed all courts and tribunals under its administrative and supervisory control to accept digitally signed copies of its daily and final orders and not insist on physical certified copies. The directive was issued through a circular dated November 25 and came into effect on November 26. The circular states that orders and judgments downloaded in PDF format from the High Court's official website, bearing a digital signature and QR code, shall be accepted by subordinate courts and tribunals. It further clarifies that the authenticity of such orders can be verified through the digital signature, QR code or any other verification mechanism provided on the High Court's official website. “The Courts shall extend full cooperation in giving effect to the digitization initiative and shall not insist upon physical certification where the order is capable of electronic verification,” the circular states. The circular was issued by order of the Chief Justice and signed by Registrar General M Chandrashekar Reddy. The communication has been addressed to all Principal District and Sessions Judges and Unit Heads across Karnataka. [Read Circular]

items.title: No relief for Tata Trusts as Bombay High Court refuses to halt Tata Sons' November 30 board meeting
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Friday refused to stay the crucial board meeting of Tata Sons scheduled for November 30, even as Tata Trusts pushed for a stay on the same. Justice Abhay Ahuja said, "We are giving you time to file reply. I am not granting any relief. Let meeting go on November 30 and the meeting is subject to the outcome of the petition." Justice Abhay Ahuja The matter will be heard next on January 21, 2027. Tata Trusts holds a 66% stake in Tata Sons. It has challenged a September 17 board resolution that reappoints N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for five years starting February 21, 2027. The board passed the resolution 4:1. Acting chair Harish Manwani cast a tie-breaking vote after Chandrasekaran abstained. Among the two Tata Trusts nominee directors, Venu Srinivasan voted for the move and Noel Tata voted against it. Tata Trusts argues the resolution is in violation of Articles 104B and 121 of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association. These rules require approval from a majority of trust-appointed directors on major decisions.
